practice_name: Batt insulation + interior poly vapor retarder (SFR)
habit_scope: AF&PA Insulation and Vapor Retarders: batt/roll full thickness in exterior walls and rafters; loose fill or roll in attic joists; 4-mil poly on the warm side under drywall. 1–2 story wood-frame. Not an R-value table. Not Title 24 (that is MarketNote mn-fontana, not this Method). ORNL foundation insulation stays in P05.
how_it_is_done: MEP rough is already in the cavities (P12). Batt or roll-type insulation goes full thickness in exterior wall stud spaces or between rafters (AF&PA Insulation).
Attic: roll or loose-fill between ceiling joists. Do not invent an R-value — none is printed in this chapter.

Batt kraft/paper facing toward the room is of little value because the usual install leaves gaps along each stud. Proper vapor protection is 4-mil (0.004 in) polyethylene film stapled to the wall studs immediately beneath the drywall or other interior finish, carefully fitted around window and door openings and behind electric outlets (AF&PA Vapor Retarders).
If plastic-foam or foil-faced sheathing is on the outside (those can act as exterior vapor retarders), the interior 4-mil poly under the finish is essential — do not skip it.

Crawl-ground 6-mil and basement-slab 6-mil over gravel are P05 (already filed). Rigid foam bonded to the inside of foundation walls is P05, not this wall/attic Method. Do not re-file ORNL foundation insulation here.
Air-seal foam/caulk sequence is not in this AF&PA chapter — Gap, do not invent. Energy inspection: Fontana Title 24 is a hold on this phase as MarketNote mn-fontana, not a Utah copy, not this Method.
trades: AF&PA: job foreman, subcontractors, building inspector — no crew size
tools_equipment: Not a tool list in sources. Named: staples for the 4-mil film (no size).
inspection_hold_points: Batt/roll full thickness in exterior walls or between rafters (AF&PA Insulation).
4-mil poly stapled to studs immediately beneath drywall; fitted around window/door openings and behind electric outlets (Vapor Retarders).
If foam or foil-faced sheathing is outside, interior poly under the finish is essential.
Fontana only: Title 24 energy inspection is a hold (mn-fontana MarketNote) — not a Utah copy, not this Method.
when_this_beats_habit: This is the AF&PA wall/attic habit. Kraft-faced batt alone is called out as not enough. Title 24 is not a competing Method.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Relying on kraft facing. Skipping interior poly when foam/foil sheathing is outside. Inventing R-values. Copying Fontana Title 24 onto Wasatch/Logan as if it were this Method. Dumping ORNL foundation foam into this phase.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They stuff batts. What they skip is the 4-mil film fitted at openings and outlets before drywall.
permit_gate: energy path on drawings where the AHJ requires it; Title 24 is Fontana MarketNote
permit_gate_notes: No R-table in AF&PA. Fontana Title 24 2025 is mn-fontana, a P13 hold, not a Method. Confirm with AHJ.
risk_if_swapped_late: Poly is under the drywall. Drywall before the film is a tear-off. Book did not name dollars.
plain_language_summary: On the 2-story stick house, after MEP rough, batts go full thickness in the walls. Attic gets roll or loose fill. Then 4-mil plastic on the warm side, stapled to the studs, fitted around windows and behind outlets, right before drywall. The paper on the batt is not enough. Fontana Title 24 is a hold on this phase — a MarketNote, not a Utah copy, not this Method. Do not invent R-values.
spanish_summary: En la casa de 2 pisos, después del rough, los batts van a espesor completo en los muros. El ático lleva rollo o relleno suelto. Luego plástico de 4 mil en el lado caliente, engrapado a los postes, recortado en ventanas y detrás de salidas, antes del drywall. El papel del batt no basta. Title 24 en Fontana es un hold de MarketNote, no una copia de Utah, no este Method. No invente valores R.
